evidence.quote: Looking ahead, however, layoffs and reductions in hiring plans due to AI use are expected to increase, especially for workers with a college degree.
Any sustained productivity growth above 2 percent will tend to support rising real incomes and living standards without inflation pressure.
A recent study by Stanford economists found that employment has fallen about 13 percent in occupations most exposed to AI, relative to those less affected.
As a monetary policymaker, I'm hoping that AI delivers.
So far, most say this is being handled through attrition, but a number of retailers say that there is the potential for downsizing next year.
